subsystems.name: Bio-ink
subsystems.role: a printable carrier that keeps cells alive and later becomes part of the tissue.
parts: extracellular matrix proteins such as collagen or fibrin
hydrogels such as alginate for temporary support

subsystems.name: Printer and printheads
subsystems.role: deposits different inks with micrometre precision.
parts: extrusion or inkjet or laser-assisted heads

subsystems.name: Vascular network
subsystems.role: brings oxygen and nutrients to every cell; without it, tissue thicker than a few hundred micrometres dies.

subsystems.name: Maturation bioreactor
subsystems.role: keeps the construct fed, warm and mechanically exercised while it matures from a print into tissue.

subsystems.name: Inspection and quality control
subsystems.role: checks that the construct is intact, perfusable and correctly built before use.

buildSteps.title: Derive and expand cells
buildSteps.detail: Patient or donor cells are reprogrammed to a stem state, grown in large numbers, and driven toward the needed cell types — heart, liver, kidney, or the endothelial cells that will line blood vessels.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the bio-inks
buildSteps.detail: Cells are mixed with matrix proteins and hydrogels, plus a second 'sacrificial' ink that can be washed out later to leave hollow channels. Each ink must flow through a nozzle without killing the cells.

buildSteps.title: Design the tissue
buildSteps.detail: Medical scans and knowledge of the organ are turned into a digital plan that specifies where each cell type and each vessel goes.

buildSteps.title: Print layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: The printer lays down structural ink and sacrificial ink in alternating patterns, building an organ-shaped construct from the bottom up, often with several printheads working at once.

buildSteps.title: Remove the sacrificial ink
buildSteps.detail: The construct is warmed or dissolved so the sacrificial material drains away, leaving a branching network of channels roughly matching real vessels, from millimetre-scale arteries down to capillary-scale spaces.

buildSteps.title: Seed the vessels
buildSteps.detail: Endothelial cells are flowed through the channels so they stick to the walls and form a living, leak-resistant lining.

buildSteps.title: Mature in a bioreactor
buildSteps.detail: The construct is perfused with oxygen-rich medium for days to weeks; mechanical or electrical stimulation helps muscle and heart cells organise and beat or contract correctly.

buildSteps.title: Test, then connect
buildSteps.detail: Perfusion tests confirm flow, then the tissue is implanted and its vessels must join up with the patient's own blood supply — the step that decides whether the graft survives.

prerequisites.why: we can make many cell types, but consistently producing mature, functional adult cells at industrial scale is not solved.

prerequisites.tech: Bio-inks that print and then behave like tissue
prerequisites.why: materials that flow through a nozzle usually need to be soft and watery, yet real tissue must be stiff and structured.
printing channels down to the smallest vessels (a few micrometres) with a stable lining is beyond current methods.
keeping a centimetre-scale construct alive for weeks without a core dying is still difficult.
a printed organ made from donor cells would be rejected; patient-derived cells are slow and costly to produce.

pathway.milestone: bioprinted thin tissue — skin, cartilage, cornea-like layers and small patches — used in research and a few early clinical trials
pathway.unlocks: proof that printed human cells can be implanted safely.

pathway.milestone: thick, vascularised tissue blocks of a centimetre or more, used mainly for drug testing instead of animals
pathway.unlocks: a commercial reason to perfect perfusion and maturation.

pathway.milestone: simple implantable organs — blood vessels, bladder-like hollow structures, airway segments
pathway.unlocks: clinical experience with printed grafts and their blood supply.

pathway.milestone: solid organs such as kidney or liver with printed vessel trees that connect to the patient's circulation
pathway.unlocks: an alternative to donor waiting lists, if immune and vascular problems are solved.
